=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired or whorled arrangement visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced out along the stem, not clustered at the apex)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf unit consists of multiple leaflets attached to a central rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (leaflets arranged in pairs along the rachis with a single terminal leaflet)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 8 (two sets of 3 leaflets on each side plus a terminal leaflet, totaling 7; however, one leaflet appears to be missing or damaged, so estimated as 8 based on typical arrangement)

C. Leaf Morphology

    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (narrow and tapering to a point, widest near the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tip is sharply pointed)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (base is wedge-shaped, tapering to the petiole)

    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible, running parallel to each other and closely spaced)

    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible when stems are broken or damaged)
